::: {.decision}
**Your decision.** A platform has 120 qualified one-loan applicants and lenders willing to fund 80 loans. It earns 60 per funded loan and spends 20 screening each qualified application. Should it pay 300 to attract another 20 applicants or another 20 units of lending capacity?
:::

## Which side limits funded loans?


```{=html}
<figure class="ess-figure" data-essentials-figure="platform-matches">
<figcaption><strong>Find the side that limits lending</strong></figcaption><p>The first panel shows funded loans as available lending capacity rises. The second deducts screening and campaign costs under the stated assumptions.</p>
<div class="ess-chart"></div>
<p><strong>Read the graph.</strong> Why does recruiting borrowers lower contribution at the starting point?</p>
<details><summary>Check your reading</summary><p>With 80 lending slots, there are already enough applicants. The campaign adds screening and acquisition costs while funding zero additional loans. Recruiting lenders raises contribution from 2,400 to 3,300.</p></details>
</figure>
```


With identical loan sizes, a funded match requires one applicant and one unit of capacity. Baseline contribution is 80 × 60 − 120 × 20 = **2,400**. More applicants leave matches at 80. Screening costs grow by 400 and the campaign costs 300. Contribution falls to 1,700.

Attracting lenders raises matches to 100 without expanding the application pool. Contribution becomes 100 × 60 − 2,400 − 300 = **3,300**. This cross-side effect depends on lenders trusting the screening process. Report approvals, funded loans, and repeat participation separately.

## What if lenders lose confidence?

**If a weakened screening standard causes funding capacity to fall to 65, what is the cost even before defaults?**

<details><summary>Work through the decision</summary><p>Relative to the 80-match baseline, lost fees are 15 × 60 = 900 with the same screening bill. If lenders bear all defaults, their expected losses do not enter the platform’s current fee margin directly. They can still change future participation. A manager estimating lifetime profits needs cohort repayment and repeat-funding data.</p></details>


```{=html}
<section aria-label="Practice brief"><h2>Which acquisition campaign should receive the budget?</h2><details><summary>Compare your recommendation</summary><p>Acquire lending capacity under the baseline. Contribution rises from 2,400 to 3,300 because another 20 loans can be funded. Monitor funded matches and repeat lender participation alongside application counts.</p></details></section>
```

**Optional comparison.** Does adding participants create more completed matches? [ECO-05 · One hundred couriers. One hundred matches?](https://kochiuyu.github.io/micro-cases/local-matches.html)


<details class="full-course-detail"><summary>When would screening another applicant become worthwhile?</summary><p>Holding capacity fixed, an extra qualified applicant adds 60 in revenue only if a slot is available and the applicant is funded. With a screening cost of 20, the marginal contribution is 40 in that case. Once capacity binds, the same application costs 20 without adding a loan. Compare campaigns by incremental matches and subtract both screening and acquisition costs.</p></details>
